src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: Recently, North Korea claimed successful test of which type of bomb?
x: North Korea claimed a successful hydrogen (thermonuclear) bomb test in January 2016 and again in September 2017.

s: The intense heat of Sun is due to
o: all the three types of these reactions
x: The Sun's heat comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core, not fission or chemical burning.

s: What is the name of atomic bomb that was dropped on Hiroshima in 1945 by Americans?
x: 'Little Boy', a U-235 bomb, was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945; 'Fat Man' (plutonium) hit Nagasaki.

s: Hydrogen Bomb is based upon the principle of
x: The hydrogen bomb is based on uncontrolled nuclear fusion of deuterium and tritium, triggered by a fission bomb.

s: Which of the following processes is responsible for release of energy by an atomic bomb?
x: An atomic bomb releases energy by an uncontrolled nuclear fission chain reaction; fusion is the hydrogen bomb.

s: Which one of the following is not correct?
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles Darwin.
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called fusion
'Dry ice' is nothing but solid carbon dioxide
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell
x: The breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one. Darwin's evolution, dry ice = solid CO2 and Bell's telephone are all correct.

s: The difference between a nuclear reactor and an atomic bomb is that
o: no chain reaction takes place in nuclear reactor
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled
no chain reaction takes place in atomic bomb
x: Both a reactor and an atom bomb run on a fission chain reaction; in the reactor it is controlled by control rods, in the bomb it is uncontrolled.

s:
Consider the following statements: In a nuclear reactor, self-sustained chain reaction is possible, because
I. more neutrons are released in each of the fission reactions.
II. the neutrons immediately take part in the fission process. Science and Technology PMF IAS S&T – 56
III. the fast neutrons are slowed down by Graphite.
IV. every neutron released in the fission reaction initiates further fission. Which of these statements are correct?
x: I and III are correct: each fission releases more neutrons, and graphite slows fast neutrons so they cause further fission. II and IV are wrong: neutrons are not all absorbed at once and not every neutron causes a new fission.

s: The stars receive their energy from which of the following?
x: Stars get their energy from nuclear fusion, mainly hydrogen fusing into helium, not from fission.

s: Which one of the following is not correct :
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles Dar-
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called
‘Dry ice’ is nothing but solid carbon dioxide
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell
x: The breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one. The other three statements are correct.

s: Otto Hahn discovered atom bomb by the principle of –
x: Otto Hahn (with Fritz Strassmann, 1938-39) discovered nuclear fission, the principle of the atom bomb. 'Uranium fission' is only one case of it, and alpha or gamma radiation is decay, not fission.

s: The principle of atomic bomb is based on –
x: The atomic bomb works by uncontrolled nuclear fission; fusion is the principle of the hydrogen bomb.

s: Hydrogen bomb was developed by :
x: Edward Teller is called the father of the hydrogen bomb (first US test, November 1952). Oppenheimer led the fission bomb project.

s: What was the fissionable material used in the bombs dropped at Nagasaki (Japan) in the year 1945 ?
x: 'Fat Man', dropped on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, used plutonium-239; 'Little Boy' at Hiroshima used U-235.

s: Which one of the following is incorrect?
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called
Dry ice is nothing but solid Carbon dioxide
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell
x: The breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one.

s: Hydrogen bomb is based on the principle of –
x: The hydrogen bomb works by uncontrolled fusion of deuterium and tritium into helium. Controlled reactions describe reactors, and fission describes the atom bomb.

s: The principle of atom bomb is based on –
x: The atom bomb relies on uncontrolled nuclear fission of uranium or plutonium. Fusion is the principle of the hydrogen bomb.

s: The working principle of atom bomb is nuclear fission of uranium and the working principle of hydrogen bomb is –
o: explosion of bomb involving hydrogen gas
x: The hydrogen bomb works by nuclear fusion of deuterium (and tritium) into helium, not by fission of thorium or chemical explosions.

s: Source of Energy from the Sun is :
x: The Sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.

s: The difference between nuclear reactor and atom bomb is that :
o: There is no chain reaction in nuclear reactor whereas
The chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled
The chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled
Atom bomb is based on nuclear fusion whereas in
x: Both a reactor and an atom bomb use a chain reaction; the difference is that in the reactor it is controlled.

s: The energy of Sun is released due to :
x: The Sun's energy is released by nuclear fusion (hydrogen into helium), not fission or oxidation-reduction.

s: Which statement is not associated with nuclear fission:
o: Source of energy in nuclear reactor that produces
Enormous energy is released in an atom bomb
x: Energy generation in stars comes from fusion, so it is not associated with fission. Fission is neutron-induced and powers reactors and the atom bomb.

s: Solar energy is due to
x: Solar energy comes from nuclear fusion in the Sun's core, not ionisation, fission or oxidation.

s: The first atom bomb was thrown over
x: The first atom bomb was dropped on Hiroshima (6 August 1945, Little Boy); Nagasaki followed on 9 August.

s: In which cities of Japan were atomic bomb dropped during Second World War?
x: Atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima (Little Boy) and Nagasaki (Fat Man) only.

s: Basic scientific principle behind a nuclear reactor is
x: A nuclear reactor runs on controlled nuclear fission. Uncontrolled fission is a bomb, and fusion power is still at the research stage.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The chain reaction process is used in nuclear bombs to release a vast amount of energy, but in nuclear reactors, there is no chain reaction.

II. In a nuclear reactor, the reaction is controlled, while in nuclear bombs, the reaction is uncontrolled.

III. In a nuclear reactor, all operating reactors are ‘critical’, while there is no question of ‘critically’ in case of a nuclear bomb.

IV. Nuclear reactors do not use moderators, while nuclear bombs use them.
Which of the above statements about operational principles of a nuclear reactor and a nuclear bomb is/are correct?
x: II and III are correct: a reactor's chain reaction is controlled and a running reactor is 'critical' (self-sustaining). I is wrong because reactors do use a chain reaction, and IV is wrong because reactors, not bombs, use moderators.

s: The source of energy of the sun is
x: The Sun runs on nuclear fusion (hydrogen into helium), not fission or photoelectric processes.

s: Hydrogen bomb is based on
x: The hydrogen bomb is based on nuclear fusion of deuterium and tritium, triggered by a fission bomb.

s: Nuclear fission is caused by the impact of
x: Fission starts when a neutron hits a heavy nucleus such as U-235, which splits and releases 2-3 more neutrons. Protons and electrons do not trigger it.

s: The difference between a nuclear reactor and atomic bomb is that
o: no chain reaction takes place in nuclear reactor is not controlled.
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is controlled.
the chain reaction in nuclear reactor is not controlled.
no-chain reaction takes place in atomic bomb while it takes place in nuclear reactor.
x: In a reactor the chain reaction is controlled by moderators and control rods; in an atom bomb it is uncontrolled. Both involve chain reactions.

s: Hydrogen bomb is based on
x: The hydrogen bomb is based on nuclear fusion; the atom bomb is the one based on fission.

s: Which one of the following reactions is the main cause of the energy radiation from the sun?
x: The Sun radiates energy from fusion reactions (hydrogen into helium) in its core.

s: Which one of the following is not correct?
o: Theory of evolution was propounded by Charles Darwin.
The breaking apart of the nucleus of an atom is called fusion.
' Dry ice ' is nothing but solid carbon dioxide.
Telephone was invented by Graham Bell.
x: Breaking apart of a nucleus is fission, not fusion, so statement b is the incorrect one. Fusion is the joining of light nuclei.

s: The mass number of a nucleus is :
o: the sum of the numbers of neutrons and protons
the total mass of neutrons and protons
always more than the atomic weight
always less than its atomic number
x: Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons (the nucleon count). It is a count, not the total mass, and it is not always more or less than other quantities.

s: The atoms, in which the number of protons is same but the number of neutrons is different, are known as –
x: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons are isotopes. Isobars share the mass number, isotones the neutron number.

s: The isoneutronic group, in the following, is :
x: Isoneutronic (isotone) nuclides have the same neutron number: 6C14 (14-6), 7N15 (15-7) and 8O16 (16-8) all have 8 neutrons. In option a the neutrons are 6, 7 and 8.

s: Isotopes is that nuclei of atomic nucleus in which –
o: Number of neutrons is same but number of protons is
Number of protons is same but number of neutrons is
Number of both protons and neutrons is same
Number of both protons and neutrons is different
x: Isotopes have the same number of protons (atomic number) but different numbers of neutrons. Same neutrons, different protons describes isotones.

s: The number of neutrons in the nucleus of plutonium nuclide (94Pu242) is :
x: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 242 - 94 = 148.

s: Constituents of atomic nucleus are –
x: The nucleus is made of protons and neutrons (the nucleons); electrons move around it in shells.

s: Isotopes are those atoms of the same element which have–
o: Atomic mass is same but atomic number is different
Atomic mass is different but atomic number is same
Atomic number and atoms mass both are same
x: Isotopes of an element have the same atomic number but a different atomic mass (mass number), because their neutron counts differ.

s: Isotopes of an element differ in :
x: Isotopes share the atomic number (protons and electrons) but differ in mass number, because their neutron counts differ.

s:
With reference to Isotopes, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Atoms with identical atomic numbers but different atomic mass numbers are known as isotopes.
2. Protium, Deuterium and Tritium are isotopes of carbon.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code :
x: Statement 1 is correct: isotopes have the same atomic number and different mass numbers. Statement 2 is wrong: protium, deuterium and tritium are isotopes of hydrogen, not carbon.

s: The Nucleus of Helium has –
x: A helium nucleus (the alpha particle) has two protons and two neutrons.

s: Heavy water is that water –
o: The temperature of which is kept constant at 4°C
In which insoluble salts of Calcium and Potassium
In which isotopes takes place of Hydrogen
In which isotopes takes place of Oxygen
x: In heavy water (D2O) deuterium, an isotope of hydrogen, takes the place of ordinary hydrogen. Oxygen is unchanged.

s: The heaviest natural element is ?
x: Uranium (Z = 92) is the heaviest element found naturally in significant amounts. Gold, mercury and calcium are much lighter.

s: Atomic number of an atom gives the number of which of the following?
x: The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus (equal to the electrons only in a neutral atom).

s: Isotopes of an element have ……… .
x: Isotopes of an element differ in their number of neutrons. They have the same atomic number and the same chemical properties.

s: Electrons in the highest energy level of an atom are called
x: Electrons in the outermost (highest energy) shell are valence electrons. 'Valence' or 'orbital' protons do not exist.

s: An element has an atomic weight of W and an atomic number of N. The number of protons in the nucleous of its atom is
x: The number of protons equals the atomic number, N. W is the mass number and W - N gives the neutrons.

s: Atomic mass of an element is equal to the sum of number of
x: The atomic mass (mass number) of an element is the sum of its protons and neutrons; electrons add almost nothing.

s: Atoms of different elements have
o: same atomic number and same electronic configuration.
different atomic number and same electronic configuration.
different atomic number and different number of valence electrons.
same number of electrons and neutrons.
x: Atoms of different elements have different atomic numbers and so different electronic configurations and numbers of valence electrons.

s: Mass number is always equal to ……..
o: sum of number of protons and number of electrons
sum of number of protons and number of neutrons
x: Mass number is always the sum of protons and neutrons.

s: Which one among the following is the most appropriate statement with respect to the atomic weight of an element?
o: The atomic weight of an element is the sum total of the number of protons and neutrons present in the atom of an element.
Unlike mass number, the atomic weight of an element can be a fraction.
The atomic weight of an element is a whole number.
The atomic weight of all the atoms in an element is the same.
x: Atomic weight is the average mass of an element's isotopes, so it can be a fraction (chlorine 35.5), whereas the mass number is always a whole number.

s: The atoms of the elements having same difference between mass number and atomic number are called …………… .
x: Mass number minus atomic number gives the neutrons; atoms with the same neutron number are isotones.

s: Isobars have …… .
o: same mass numbers but different atomic numbers.
different mass numbers but same atomic numbers.
x: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers (3H and 3He).

s: Scattering of α-particles by a thin gold foil suggests the presence of
o: positively charged nucleus at the centre of an atom
x: Most alpha particles passed through the gold foil but a few bounced back, showing a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom (Rutherford).

s: The most of the mass of the atom can be found in
x: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus carry almost all the atom's mass; electrons are about 1/1837 of a proton.

s: An atom has 7 electrons in its M-shell and contains 18 neutrons in its nucleus. What is its mass number?
x: 7 electrons in the M-shell means 2 + 8 + 7 = 17 electrons, so 17 protons. Mass number = 17 + 18 = 35.

s: The force of attraction between an electron revolving around the nucleus and the nucleus is an … force.
x: The negatively charged electron and the positively charged nucleus attract by the electric (electrostatic) force; gravity is negligible at that scale.

s: Neutron is a fundamental particle carrying
o: a charge of + 1 and mass of 1 unit.
no charge and a mass of 1 unit.
a charge of - 1 and a mass of 1 unit.
x: A neutron has no charge and a mass of about 1 atomic mass unit (slightly more than a proton).

s: Charge on proton is equal to the charge on ………… .
x: A positron carries +1 charge, the same as a proton. The electron is negative, the neutron neutral and the alpha particle +2.

s: Chemical properties of Isotopes
x: Isotopes have the same number of protons and electrons, so their chemical properties must be the same; only physical properties such as mass differ.

s:
Which of the following statements with regard to isotopes and isobars is/are correct?

I. Isotopes have same mass number.

II. Isobars have same atomic number.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Both statements are reversed: isotopes share the atomic number (not the mass number) and isobars share the mass number (not the atomic number). So neither is correct.

s: An atom of carbon has 6 protons. Its mass number is 12. How many neutrons are present in an atom of carbon?
x: Neutrons = mass number - protons = 12 - 6 = 6.

s: The number of electrons and neutrons in an element is 18 and 20 respectively. Its mass number is
x: A neutral atom has as many protons as electrons (18), so the mass number = 18 + 20 = 38.

s: Which one of the following statements about the properties of neutrons is not correct?
o: Neutron mass is almost equal to proton mass
Neutrons are located inside the atomic nuclei
Neutrons revolve around the atomic nuclei
x: Neutrons sit inside the nucleus; they do not revolve around it (electrons do). Their mass is almost equal to a proton's and they have zero charge.

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s: The most common method Uranium enrichment is?
x: Uranium (as UF6 gas) is enriched mostly in gas centrifuges, which separate U-235 from the slightly heavier U-238. Distillation, ionisation and calcification are not used.

s: The fuel used in the nuclear reactors is
x: Uranium (U-235) is the fuel of nuclear reactors. Thorium is only fertile and must first be bred into U-233; radium is not a reactor fuel and 'nuclear water' does not exist.

s: Material most commonly used in nuclear power plants is
x: Uranium-235 is the fissile fuel most commonly used in nuclear power plants. Plutonium is used in fewer reactors, thorium is only fertile and radium is not a fuel.

s: Which of the following radio active elements is used to make nuclear fission reaction?
x: Uranium (its fissile isotope U-235) is the element split in nuclear fission reactors and bombs. Thorium is fertile and must first become U-233; barium is a fission product, not a fuel.

s: Which nuclear fuel is produced when thorium is bombarded with neutrons?
x: Th-232 is fertile; when it absorbs a neutron it turns into fissile Uranium-233. Hard water, hydrogen sulphide and heavy water are not nuclear fuels.

s: What nuclear fuel does bombarding Thorium with neutrons produce?
x: Bombarding Thorium-232 with neutrons converts it into fissile Uranium-233, the basis of India's thorium fuel cycle. The other options are not nuclear fuels.

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to the enrichment of Uranium:

I. Uranium enrichment refers to increasing the percentage of U-238 (the fissile isotope) through the process of isotope separation.

II. Weapons-grade Uranium has to be enriched to a maximum of 20 percent of the fissile isotope.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement I is wrong: enrichment raises the share of U-235, the fissile isotope, not U-238 (which is fertile). Statement II is wrong: 20% is the ceiling for research reactors, while weapons-grade uranium is about 90% U-235. So neither is correct.

s: Which one of the following elements is essential for the construction of nuclear reactors?
x: Zirconium alloys clad the fuel rods because they resist corrosion and absorb very few neutrons. Cobalt, nickel and tungsten are not essential reactor materials.

s: Which Uranium isotope is used in nuclear power plants to produce electricity?
x: U-235 is the fissile isotope burnt in nuclear power plants; natural uranium has only about 0.7% of it. U-233 is bred from thorium, while U-234 and U-239 are not used as fuel.

s: Identify the mineral not associated with atomic power –
x: Chromium has no role in atomic power. Monazite is the ore of thorium, thorium is a fertile fuel and beryllium (oxide) is a moderator and a prescribed atomic substance.

s: Which fuel is used by Nuclear reactors in India ?
x: Indian PHWRs burn natural uranium, which is about 99.3% U-238 with 0.7% U-235, so U-238 is the only printed option that fits. U-270 and U-500 do not exist and gasohol is a motor fuel.

s: Which of the following element is not included as a nuclear fuel–
x: Cadmium is not a fuel: it absorbs neutrons and is used in control rods. Thorium, plutonium and uranium are nuclear fuels (thorium after breeding).

s: Enriched Uranium is –
o: Uranium sticks laid in particular shell
Natural uranium in which radioactive U235 isotope is
mixture of natural uranium and thorium
x: Enriched uranium is natural uranium in which the share of the U-235 isotope has been raised by isotope separation. It is not a thorium mixture or coated sticks.

s: Which is not used as Atomic fuel?
x: Lead is not a nuclear fuel. Uranium and plutonium are fissile, and thorium is fertile and can be bred into U-233.

s: Which of the following is not a fuel element?
x: Helium is an inert gas and not a nuclear fuel element. Uranium and thorium are nuclear fuels; radium is radioactive but the clear odd one out is helium.

s: Which one of the following can not be used as a nuclear fuel?
x: Calcium is not a nuclear fuel. Uranium-235 and plutonium-239 are fissile, and thorium is bred into U-233.

s: Which metal can be used for producing electricity?
x: Uranium is the metal used to produce electricity, as nuclear fuel in power plants. Iron, copper and aluminium only carry or build things.

s: Which of the following uranium isotope is used in nuclear reactor for generation of electricity?
x: U-235 is the fissile uranium isotope used to generate electricity. U-233 is bred from thorium, while U-334 does not exist and U-239 is not a fuel.

s: Which one of the following is a good nuclear fuel?
x: Plutonium-239 is fissile, so it is a good nuclear fuel. U-238 is only fertile (it must first become Pu-239), neptunium is not a fuel and 'thorium-236' is not the fertile Th-232. (The old app notes said the APPSC 2007 key was U-238; that key was not verified and is factually wrong.)

s: The main element in the Ore Pitchblende is
x: Pitchblende (uraninite, UO2/U3O8) is the chief ore of uranium. Monazite, not pitchblende, is the thorium ore.

s: Which one of the following mineral is used as a fuel in nuclear power stations?
x: Pitchblende is the main uranium ore, and uranium is the fuel of nuclear power stations. Bauxite (aluminium), quartz and feldspar are not nuclear fuels.

s: Which one of the following is not radioactive ?
x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive. Astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements and tritium is a radioactive isotope of hydrogen.

s: Radioactive substance emits –
x: An unstable nucleus can emit alpha, beta and gamma radiation, so all three.

s: Emission of β-particle from an atom
o: increases the number of protons in the atom.
increases the number of neutrons in the atom.
decreases the number of proton in the atom.
does not change the number of neutrons and protons in an atom.
x: In beta-minus emission a neutron changes into a proton and an electron, which is emitted, so the number of protons rises by one.

s: What is end product of nuclear fission of Uranium?
x:
Printed key / books: Lead (end of the uranium decay series). Strictly, nuclear fission of uranium yields barium, krypton and other fission fragments, not lead (PMF S&T Part 4 p.24).
Lead is the stable end product of uranium's radioactive decay series (U-238 to Pb-206), which is the reading the key takes. Fission itself splits uranium into lighter nuclei such as barium and krypton; radium and thorium are intermediate decay products and plutonium is bred from U-238.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which of the following is not a radioactive series?
x: There is no 'carbon series'. Thorium, actinium and uranium are natural radioactive decay series, and neptunium is an artificial series.

s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of:
o: Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single positive charge
x: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons), so its mass is almost that of a helium atom; electrons weigh very little. Two protons alone would be only half that mass.

s: Which of the following particles has zero charge?
x: The neutrino has zero charge (and almost no mass). The positron is +1, the electron -1 and the alpha particle +2.

s: Which of the following is not a sub-atomic particle?
x: The basic sub-atomic particles are the neutron, proton and electron. A deuteron is the nucleus of deuterium (a proton plus a neutron), not a basic sub-atomic particle.

s: Which of the following carries a negative charge?
x: Beta particles are fast electrons and carry a negative charge. Alpha particles are positive, while X-rays and gamma rays are uncharged radiation.

s: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 10 days; it means there will be :
o: complete decay of substance in 20 days
complete decay of substance in 40 days
decay of 3/4 part of substance in 20 days
decay of 1/4 part of substance in 5 days
x: After one half-life (10 days) half remains, after two (20 days) a quarter remains, so 3/4 has decayed in 20 days. A substance never decays completely.

s: The half-life of a radioactive element is 5 years then the fraction of the radioactive substance that remains after 20 years is –
x: 20 years is 4 half-lives of 5 years, so (1/2)^4 = 1/16 of the substance remains.

s: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of –
o: Nucleus of an atom of helium
Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons, as each positron carries a single
x: An alpha particle is two protons and two neutrons, i.e. the nucleus of a helium atom, so its mass equals that of a helium nucleus.

s:
With reference to the radioactivity, which of the following statements is/are correct ?
1. Radioactivity is a nuclear property.
2. Hydrogen bomb is prepared on the principle of nuclear fission.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
Codes :
x: Statement 1 is correct: radioactivity is a nuclear property. Statement 2 is wrong: the hydrogen bomb works on fusion, not fission.

s: Which particle is free of charge?
x: The neutron carries no charge. The alpha particle (+2) and proton (+1) are positive, the electron negative.

s: Radioactivity is measured by –
x: Radioactivity is detected and measured with a Geiger (Geiger-Muller) counter. A hydrometer measures density, a seismometer earthquakes and an ammeter current.

s: Which among the following is a positively charged particle emitted by a radioactive element?
o: More than one of the above
x: Alpha rays are positively charged helium nuclei emitted by radioactive elements. Beta rays and cathode rays are electrons (negative).

s: Which of the following is not a radio active element?
x: Zirconium (Z = 40) is not radioactive, whereas astatine and francium are heavy radioactive elements and tritium is a radioactive hydrogen isotope.

s: Beta rays emitted by a radioactive material are
o: the electrons orbiting around the nucleus.
x: Beta rays are electrons (or positrons) emitted from the nucleus, so they are charged particles. They are not orbital electrons, not neutral and not electromagnetic radiation (that is gamma).

s: Half-life of a radioactive element is 10 days. What does it mean?
o: Element will be completely disintigrate in 20 days.
Element will be completely disintigrate in 40 days.
3/4th part of element will disintigrate in 20 days.
1/4th part of element will distintigarate in 5 days.
x: After 10 days half remains and after 20 days a quarter, so 3/4 has disintegrated in 20 days. The element never fully disintegrates.

s: In an observation, α-particles, β-particles and γ-rays have same energies. Their penetrating power in a given medium in increasing order will be
x: Alpha is stopped by paper, beta by a few mm of aluminium and gamma only by lead or concrete, so penetrating power rises in the order alpha, beta, gamma.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: In May, 2017, the Central Cabinet decided to launch 10 indigenous nuclear reactors of the following type as part of a mega project?
x: In May 2017 the Union Cabinet approved 10 indigenous 700 MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors to be built in fleet mode. PWRs and FBRs were not part of that decision; Magnox is a British design.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: A moderator is used in nuclear reactors in order to
o: slow down the speed of neutrons
x: A moderator slows fast neutrons to thermal speed so that U-235 can capture them and fission. It does not add, absorb or accelerate neutrons; absorbing is the job of control rods.

s: ___ is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors.
x: Heavy water (D2O) is a moderator: it slows neutrons while absorbing very few of them. Hydrogen peroxide, dihydrogen and CFCs are not moderators.

s: Which one of the following is used as moderator in a nuclear reactor ?
x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Heavy water. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Heavy water slows neutrons without absorbing many, so it is the classic moderator. Ordinary (light) water is a moderator too, in PWRs and BWRs, which is why the book lists '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

s: Which one of the following is used as a moderator in the nuclear reactor?
x:
Printed key / most books: (b) Graphite. Strictly, (d) ordinary water is also a moderator, in light-water reactors (PMF S&T Part 4 p.38).
Graphite slows neutrons and is a standard moderator. Ordinary water is also a moderator in light-water reactors, which is why the book prints '(b) & (d)'. Thorium and radium are not moderators.

s: Graphite is used in the nuclear reactor as –
x: Graphite slows fast neutrons, so it serves as a moderator; it is not the fuel. Its lubricant use is outside reactors.

s: The moderator used in nuclear reactor is :
x: Heavy water, D2O (deuterium oxide), is the moderator. U2O, Na2O and Cl2O are not moderators.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s:
Match the following:
Column A: i. Fission ii. Control rod iii. Coolant iv. Fuel v. Reactor core
Column B:
a. Where fuel, moderator and control rods are located
b. Splitting of heavy atomic nuclei to release energy
c. Transfer heat from the reactor core
d. Splitting of heavy atomic nuclei to release energy
e. Substance that slows down neutrons
x: Only option b has fission-splitting of nuclei (b), coolant-transfers heat (c) and reactor core-where fuel, moderator and control rods are located (a). The printed list is garbled: 'e' (slows neutrons) describes a moderator, not a control rod, which absorbs neutrons, and 'd' repeats 'splitting'.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: What is the function of moderator in a nuclear reactor?
x: A moderator slows down neutrons so that they can cause further fission. Absorbing heat is the coolant's job; control rods regulate the rate.

s: What happens if the control rods are not used in a nuclear reactor?
o: Chain process would go out of bounds
The reactor will be slow to act
The reactor will continue to work as it is
x: Control rods absorb surplus neutrons; without them the chain reaction would go out of bounds rather than stop or slow down.
